extracted.intended_audience: cartoonists, comics writers, and humorists studying or emulating Jules Feiffer's neurotic-monologue style
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for creating satirical, therapy-inflected comic strips built around literate monologues — typically a single speaker whose speech reveals insecurities and unwinds across minimal, line-focused panels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Satirical comic strip with very literate captions
rubrics_metrics.description: Satirical comic strip with very literate captions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signature Form: the strip is satirical rather than purely gag-based; captions are literary in diction and sensibility. Emphasize wit, irony and educated phrasing rather than one-line punchlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monologue-based verbal elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Verbal elements take form of monologues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The humor is carried primarily in extended speech rather than dialogic banter or short gags. Monologues allow free-association and internal argument; they should sustain interest across panels by shifting tone and revealing inwardness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single speaker across panels
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there a single speaker across panels?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often a single character speaks through multiple panels, providing continuity and allowing the reader to track shifting emotions and escalating self-revelation. Check that the voice remains distinct and coherent as it moves through beats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monologue reveals more than speaker realizes
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the monologue reveal more than the speaker realizes?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dramatic irony is central: the speaker unintentionally exposes insecurities, contradictions, or desires. The writing should let subtext leak out even while the speaker insists otherwise; avoid explicit self-awareness by the speaker.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language is literary and therapeutic
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draw on therapy-talk and literate phrasing: language may echo psychiatric/therapy-speak (therapeutic culture) and elevated diction. The tone should feel urbane and inward-looking, reflecting how therapy-talk reshapes everyday speech.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eschew gag/punchline structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Eschewed gag format of vaudeville tradition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid the tight setup-punchline model; prefer an unfolding interior logic where humor comes from recognition and psychological exposure rather than a surprise one-liner. The piece should feel more like an essayistic unraveling than a joke sequence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimal panels; line-art focus on speech
rubrics_metrics.description: Are panels minimal (line-art focus on speech)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visuals should be stripped to essentials so the reader's attention rests on the monologue: minimal backgrounds, economy of detail, and a focus on facial/body reaction as punctuation. Use sparing imagery to support — not compete with — the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Borderless frames and scratchy, loose drawing
rubrics_metrics.description: Borderless frames. Scratchy lines. 'Jangly looseness of a Rorschach test or psychiatrist's notepad.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt a loose, sketchy line style and often borderless panels to create an intimate, stream-of-consciousness feel. The visual looseness should suggest spontaneity and psychological rawness, reinforcing free-association in the monologue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panels as beats of unwinding self-deception
rubrics_metrics.description: Each panel is a beat in their unwinding self-deception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure the strip so each panel functions as a discrete beat that progresses the speaker's unraveling or rationalization. The sequence should feel like a chain of small revelations that cumulatively reveal the speaker's delusion or insecurity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character is sympathetic and pathetic
rubrics_metrics.description: The character is sympathetic AND pathetic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance empathy and embarrassment: the speaker should be recognizable and elicit compassion while also appearing ridiculous or pitiable. Avoid caricature that kills sympathy, and avoid mawkishness that removes humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience laughs and identifies with speaker's blindness
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the audience laugh AND identify with the speaker's blindness?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful strips produce both humor and identification: readers should see themselves in the neuroses on display while also finding the situation comic. Aim for self-recognition rather than purely mocking the speaker.

rubrics_metrics.name: Themes: intimate, social, and existential preoccupations
rubrics_metrics.description: Themes include relationships, sex, depression, family troubles, current events, existential angst.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose subject matter that is personal yet culturally resonant — romantic/sexual angst, family dynamics, mental health, topical social commentary, and existential worries. These themes allow the monologue to oscillate between private confession and public context.
